subject: Showing specific lines in parallel coordinates plot

messages.author: 8d9b7a8e9ed23226
messages.subject: Showing specific lines in parallel coordinates plot
parts:
Hi,

I have the following parallel coordinates plot (using the built-in
dataset mtcars):

ggpcp(mtcars, vars=names(mtcars[2:6])) + geom_point(aes(colour=mpg),
size=I(5), alpha = I(0.3)) + geom_line(aes(colour=mpg), alpha=I(0.5))

But, say, I want to show only the lines for the "Volvo 142E" and the
"Fiat X1-9". How should I modify the geom_line to do this?

Thanks.

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Showing specific lines in parallel coordinates plot
parts:
I think you need to subset the data that you're giving ggplot in order to get only the lines that you want. This seems to work...  

log.vec<-rownames(mtcars) == "Volvo 142E"|rownames(mtcars) == "Fiat X1-9"

ggpcp(mtcars[log.vec,], vars=names(mtcars[2:6])) + geom_point(aes(colour=mpg),
size=I(5), alpha = I(0.3)) + geom_line(aes(colour=mpg), alpha=I(0.5))
Brandon

parts:
Ah, that is more clear. 

Every time I try and specify a subset of data for an individual geom it gives me the following error. 
> ggpcp(mtcars, vars=names(mtcars[2:6])) + geom_point(data=mtcars, aes(colour=mpg),
+ size=I(5), alpha = I(0.3))
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'variable' not found

Even if the data specified is the same data. 

Worse case scenario, you'll end up doing what ggpcp() does inside to your dataset before making a plot with ggplot. A little more complex than one would like...

?ggpcp() 

says it uses melt() to get a dataframe and likely when you use it, it forces the following geoms to use the same melted frame, which means that subsetting the original frame confuses it. At least that's my interpretation. Know how to melt?

Brandon

messages.author: b3ca0c52e87f982f
messages.subject: Re: Showing specific lines in parallel coordinates plot
parts:
Hi there,

I'm not familiar with the ggpcp() function. I thus might have missed
more concise ways to do it. However, the following code seems to do
what you want.

require(ggplot2)

# create a new var with the car names
mtcars$car<-rownames(mtcars)

# melt the the data frame and rescale it
# this is identical to the transformations done by the ggpcp()
function
mmtcars <- melt(mtcars, measure = 2:6)
mmtcars <- ddply(mmtcars, 'variable', transform, value=
rescaler(value, type='range'))

# plot it
ggplot(aes(x= variable, y = value, col=mpg), data=mmtcars) +
geom_point(size=I(5), alpha = I(0.3)) +
geom_line(aes(group=car), alpha=I(0.5), data=subset(mmtcars, car %in%
c('Volvo 142E', 'Fiat X1-9')))

HTH

Matthieu

Matthieu Dubois
Post-doctoral fellow, National Fund for Scientific Research (Belgium)
